subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (recap and next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@finova.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (recap and next steps)

Hi Jenna / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we discussed and agreed as next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of requirements (from your notes):
- Latency targets: p95 & p99 per region; streaming first-byte SLA for chat.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline throughput for batch generation, peak burst characteristics, and per-user concurrency limits.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming necessary for your UX (first-byte and per-token latencies matter).
- Regional routing/data residency: EU data must remain in EU for storage and processing; APAC prefers local residency where possible. Failover behavior and fallback to US must be explicit.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence + audit logs retention requirements.

Lib SLO targets (proposed by Redwood during call):
- US (primary): p95 <= 150ms for short requests (<=512 tokens); p99 <= 350ms.
- EU: p95 <= 180ms; p99 <= 420ms.
- APAC: p95 <= 220ms; p99 <= 600ms (higher tail due to cross-region RTT).
- Streaming: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) <= 100ms in-region; per-token median <= 40ms for 1-2 token chunks.
- Throughput: sustained baseline 200 requests/sec across the fleet with capacity for 1,200 req/sec burst for up to 5 minutes.
- Concurrency: expected 50 concurrent streaming connections per instance pool; autoscale target to 500 concurrent streams across the region.

Notes on routing & residency:
- We recommend regional routing (US/EU/APAC) with strict routing for EU data: requests originating from EU addresses must be served from EU region endpoints; logs and any persisted derived data stored in EU.
- APAC: recommend local region if you require <250ms p95; otherwise APAC -> nearest US west fallback with clear SLAs.
- Cross-region backups and aggregated metrics can be replicated to US for analytics if you sign the data transfer agreement; otherwise we can keep all telemetry in-region.

Action items / next steps:
1) Marissa: send an updated SLO matrix (attached) and a regional routing diagram by EOD today.
2) Aditya: provide a perf test plan and recommended load shape to validate the targets (including streaming microbenchmarks).
3) Dev: confirm retention window for audit logs and the minimum evidence set for SOC 2 (we discussed 13 months).
4) Jenna/Carlos: confirm whether Finova will allow EU->US telemetry replication or require strict in-region analytics.

Attachments: redwood_perf_sla_matrix.xlsx, regional_routing_diagram.png

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finova.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (recap and next steps)

Thanks Marissa — this looks right to me. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) APAC: we need to avoid cross-border storage for any PII; if logs contain identifiers they must be redacted or kept only in-region. Telemetry for aggregate metrics is ok to replicate (after redaction).
2) Streaming: our UX requires TTFB <= 120ms in-region; 100ms would be ideal but 120ms is our minimum. Per-token latency should stay under 60ms for 1-token streaming.
3) Throughput: the 1,200 req/sec burst is acceptable; peak windows are usually 3-4 minutes during certain trading hours.

Next steps from us:
- We’ll confirm the telemetry policy by EOD Monday (Apr 26).
- Would like Aditya to propose the perf test plan timeline (approx when you can run an in-region test).

Quick note — can you call out any differences in SLOs if we choose Dedicated vs Hosted? We expect stricter tail latencies on Dedicated but want to understand operational tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Jenna
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
jenna.park@finova.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (recap and next steps)

Thanks — quick technical notes and what I'll deliver for the perf plan: 

- Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated (reserved capacity) gives you pinned GPU pools per region which reduces cross-tenant variance and improves P99 tail by ~15-25% depending on model. Hosted can meet p95 numbers easily with our autoscaling and smart batching but p99 tail is more variable at very high concurrency. We'll include both scenarios in the plan.

- Perf test plan (deliverable items):
  * Test harness that runs in-region synthetic workloads (US/EU/APAC) using your sample prompts.
  * Streaming microbenchmarks: measure TTFB and per-token latency for 50, 200, 500 concurrent streams.
  * Load tests: sustained 200 req/s baseline; burst profile 1,200 req/s for 5 minutes.
  * Measurement: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end request latency, TTFB distribution, and token throughput.

- Data residency implementation notes:
  * We can enforce strict in-region processing for EU by routing to EU-only control plane + storage.
  * For APAC, we recommend local Dedicated pools if you need <250ms p95 consistently.

I'll aim to share a first-cut perf plan and the harness repo link by Tue Apr 27 COB.

Regards,
Aditya
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Marissa
